newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Erbakan gives no date for power handover.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan gives no date for power handover.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan on Monday declined to fix a date for a planned handover of power to his coalition partner to end a political crisis over Islamist activism.
But a close aide said Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, would step down in favour of government ally Tansu Ciller this week.

"The government protocol envisages that after one year the prime minister can be changed after considering the situation," Erbakan told a news conference in response to persistent questions on whether he was to stand down.
"It is not very important who has what position. Whenever we have to do something together, we shall do it together."

His coalition ally the True Path Party has threatened to pull out of the government if its leader Ciller is not made prime minister by June 18 under a power-sharing deal the two partners agreed on one year ago.
"We will hand over the prime minister's post this week," State Minister Abdullah Gul, an Erbakan aide, told Reuters.
Erbakan and Deputy Prime Minister Ciller earlier announced they would swap jobs by the end of this month and form a caretaker government to go for early elections.
A power transfer and early polls would need to be approved by the president and parliament, where the coalition now lacks a majority after a series of defections.
Erbakan has been under intense pressure in recent months in an anti-Islamist campaign, led by the secularist army.
The Turkish press said on Monday that members of Ciller's pro-Western party, uneasy at keeping the Islamists in government, were trying to scuttle the proposed power transfer at the last minute.
But Erbakan expressed confidence on Monday that he would win the support of eight deputies from a far-right party to push through his plans in the 550-seat assembly.
"When we pool our resources we have a majority of 283 in parliament," he told reporters at the news conference, called to present the results of a weekend summit of eight Moslem nations.
Far-right powerbroker Muhsin Yazicioglu has said his party was as yet undecided on whether to use its eight votes to back the government in parliament, without actually joining the coalition.
